title: Data Access Request
text:
Researchers who wish to obtain restricted, de-identified datasets are invited to submit a request using the form below. You must provide your institutional email address and research purpose before we can evaluate your request.


Contact Information

Name * 
Institution and Department * 
Position (e.g., PhD student, Postdoc, Professor) * 
Institutional Email Address * 

Project Details

Project Title * 
Short Abstract (150–300 words) *

Main Research Questions or Hypotheses *

Planned Analyses (e.g., multilevel models, longitudinal models) *



Data Needs

Which dataset(s) are you requesting? *

Which modules or variable groups are essential?

Any planned linkages with external datasets?



Ethics and Governance

Has your project obtained (or will it obtain) ethical approval? *

Name of ethics committee and reference number (if available) 
Data protection measures at your institution *



Outputs and Dissemination

Intended outputs (e.g., journal article, thesis, report) *

Expected timeline * 

Submission


Once submitted, your request will be emailed to the coordinating team for review. You will receive a confirmation and follow-up via email.

Submit Request


 After internal review, we will inform you whether:


Your request is approved (subject to signing the Data Use Agreement),


Additional information is required, or


The request cannot be granted.

title: Welcome
text: Welcome to the Societal Needs Data Hub, a central repository for large-scale datasets at the intersection of psychology and society.  The Data Hub’s mission is to bridge psychological science with societal challenges by fostering collaboration across research domains, practitioners, and policy actors, an essential endeavour both in times of crisis and for society’s long-term resilience.

title: Welcome
text:
Layers of accessibility






🔓 Layer 1: Public Access





Openly available to everyone:

Study documentation and protocols

Codebooks and variable lists

Aggregated statistics and dashboards

Analysis scripts and tutorials

Use this layer to:

Explore what the projects are about

Understand the structure of the data

Teach & learn longitudinal analysis

Browse documentation









📝 Layer 2: Registered Access





Restricted, de-identified versions of the real data are available on request.
To apply, researchers provide:

A brief project description

Ethical approval (if applicable)

Required variables/modules

Approved users sign a Data Use Agreement, committing to:

No re-identification

No redistribution

Secure storage

Proper citation

Access is granted via private links tied to a specific dataset version.
Request data access









🔒 Layer 3: Internal Access





Full datasets, including sensitive modules and detailed identifiers, are restricted to the project consortium.
These data:

Are stored in secure private repositories

Support ongoing modelling & manuscript preparation

Are not shared externally without additional procedures

title: Methodology
text:
The Motivation Barometer and THRIVE datasets comprise cross-sectional and longitudinal data collected during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The key aims include:

Assessing changes in motivation, psychological needs, and well-being over time.
Examining responses to public communication and policy measures.
Investigating links between societal conditions, behavior and mental health.
Deriving evidence-based recommendations for future crisis preparedness and inclusive post-COVID policies.



The Motivation Barometer is a large-scale, online monitoring study that was launched on 19 March 2020, one day after the first national lockdown in Belgium (2020 - 2023). During the first ten weeks of the pandemic, daily surveys were administered, with a subset of participants followed for ten consecutive weeks. As the pandemic evolved, new waves were organized at a slower pace and adapted to emerging topics (e.g., vaccination, COVID certificate, trust, conspiracy beliefs).

Total waves: more than 110 measurement waves over roughly 2.5 years.

Total responses: nearly 484 000 completed questionnaires.

Unique participants: over 320 000 individuals.

Design: combination of cross-sectional cohorts and longitudinal panels, with targeted subsamples (e.g., students, parents, older adults, athletes, (un)vaccinated individuals).

Each wave combined a core set of variables (motivation, basic psychological needs, adherence to measures) with topical modules tailored to the phase of the pandemic (e.g., attitudes toward mandatory vaccination, perceptions of the COVID certificate, conspiracy beliefs, boredom, loneliness).



The THRIVE project (“Taking stock to foster health and trust for an inclusive post-Covid society”) is a BELSPO funded Post-Covid research programme (2023 - 2026). THRIVE explicitly builds on the Motivation Barometer by:

Consolidating and harmonizing existing Motivation Barometer waves.

Adding new post-Covid follow-up waves.

Integrating complementary qualitative and survey data.

Its core objectives are to:

Chart the social and psychological heterogeneity of the population during the COVID-19 crisis by identifying distinctive trajectories of motivation, well-being, trust, and democratic attitudes.
Examine how these trajectories relate to resilience and vulnerability, including long-term mental health outcomes.
Combine multiple disciplines and methods (health psychology, motivation psychology, social psychology, sociology; quantitative and qualitative approaches).
Identify contextual drivers (e.g., communication style, stringency of measures, trust, ideology) that feed into people’s experiences and reactions.

title: Methodology
text:
Cleaning and processing
Key steps include:

Screening for invalid responses (e.g., extremely short completion time, failed attention checks).
Handling missing data according to pre-specified rules (e.g., minimum item responses for scale scores).
Recoding and labeling variables consistently across surveys, waves and projects.
Constructing composite scores
Creating weights for selected waves to approximate Belgian population distributions in age, gender, and region.

All major processing steps are documented in reproducible R scripts, available in the GitHub repository and referenced in the tutorials.

title: Variable overview
text:
Cross-wave consistency
Where possible, constructs were measured with consistent items and response scales across waves to facilitate longitudinal analyses. Any changes in wording, scaling, or module composition are documented in the relevant codebook.

title: Motivation Barometer & THRIVE
text:
The Motivation Barometer & THRIVE dataset brings together both (sequential) cross-sectional as repeated follow-up surveys with a large panel of participants in Belgium. It follows people’s motivation, psychological functioning, and societal attitudes during and after the COVID-19 crisis and across broader societal challenges.

All variables with items can be found in the codebook
